name: MongoDB
thesis: MongoDB — the leading document database, monetized primarily through Atlas (cloud, consumption-priced). The bet rests on one macro premise: AI collapses the cost of producing software, so the world ships far more applications than the market models — and every new application is a new database workload. Atlas is usage-priced, so MongoDB captures that surge directly in consumption (not seats), with no per-developer ceiling. The thesis: (1) Atlas keeps compounding ~mid-20s% as both workload COUNT and per-workload consumption rise, (2) total revenue growth stays >=20% (it re-accelerated to ~23% in FY26 after dipping to 19% in FY25), (3) NRR holds >=115% as existing apps grow into more data, (4) the model stays strongly FCF-generative (FY26 FCF margin ~20%) even while GAAP-unprofitable BY DESIGN — SBC is ~22% of revenue, so GAAP operating margin is negative while non-GAAP is ~15%+ and FCF is real. Picks-the-platform, not the app: indifferent to which AI-built apps win, as long as they run on Mongo. Narrative kicker (not yet a tracked KPI): AI agents and AI-native apps generate machine-speed data volumes that usage pricing converts straight to revenue. Competitive reality: Postgres (+pgvector) is the default rival for AI/vector workloads and hyperscalers bundle their own document stores — MongoDB's developer experience + multi-cloud neutrality is the moat that must hold.
key_driver: Atlas consumption growth (workload count x per-workload usage), captured directly by usage-based pricing

tier_1_kpis.name: Total Revenue YoY Growth (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (consumption tailwind failing to show up)

tier_1_kpis.name: Atlas Revenue YoY Growth
tier_1_kpis.current: Atlas ~70%+ of revenue, growing ~mid-20s% (per company disclosure; backfill exact)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (core consumption engine stalling)

tier_1_kpis.name: FCF Margin (GAAP)
tier_1_kpis.current: +20.3% FY26 ($0.50B FCF) — cash-generative despite GAAP op loss

tier_2_kpis.name: SBC / Revenue
tier_2_kpis.current: ~22% FY26 (the reason GAAP op margin is negative; watch for dilution, not 'losses')

nuance.bear_case: The whole thesis is consumption-elasticity: if AI does NOT meaningfully lift application/workload creation, or if the new apps default to Postgres/pgvector and hyperscaler-native stores rather than Mongo, then Atlas growth keeps grinding toward the high-teens and the 're-acceleration' was a one-off. GAAP unprofitability + ~22%-of-revenue SBC means the equity story leans on non-GAAP and FCF — a multiple de-rate hits hard.
nuance.adversarial_take: 23% growth on a $2.5B base is good, not euphoric, and the 'more software than the market expects' premise is unfalsifiable in the short run — it shows up (or doesn't) only in sustained Atlas consumption. The live tell is whether Atlas growth and NRR stop decelerating.
nuance.stress_test: If total revenue growth slips below 15% AND NRR drops below 110% in the same year, the consumption-tailwind thesis is broken regardless of the AI narrative.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Atlas growth decelerates below 20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs
Total revenue growth falls below 15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs
FCF margin regresses below 10% (consumption economics breaking)
AI-native apps standardize on Postgres/pgvector or hyperscaler-native stores rather than Mongo

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken (catastrophic floor; the per-ticker rule at 10% is the real watch).
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

business_model_rules.narrative: Total revenue growth below 15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — the consumption/'more-software' tailwind is not materializing (FY26 ran ~23%).
Atlas revenue YoY growth below 20% for 2 consecutive Qs — the core consumption engine is stalling. (UNRESOLVED until Atlas growth is backfilled as a KPI.)
NRR below 110% — existing-application expansion (the consumption flywheel) is stalling. (UNRESOLVED until NRR is backfilled.)
FCF margin below 10% for 2 consecutive Qs — consumption economics regressing (FY26 ran ~20%); the real cash watch above the 5% catastrophic floor.
Gross margin below 62% for 2 consecutive Qs — Atlas infra pricing/cost pressure (FY26 ran ~72%).
